text: As for politeness: whoever keeps good company, and is not polite, must have formed a resolution, and take some pains not to be so; otherwise he would naturally and insensibly take the air, the address, and the turn of those he converses with.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XCIX, to his son, London, December 26, Old Style 1749
